title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: exclude specific domains from web grounding
summary: Hold: excluded domains can still appear in news and other answer types, so this is not a comprehensive citation block. The briefing also gives incomplete configuration paths, misstates the script's administrator role and data sent to web search, and asserts licensing and pricing that Microsoft does not document.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is Rolling out.
claims.quote: "status": "Rolling out"

claims.claim: The roadmap release phase is General Availability.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability"]

claims.claim: The roadmap lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant).
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.claim: The roadmap lists Desktop and Web.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Desktop", "Web"]

claims.claim: The roadmap gives September 2026 as the General Availability date.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "September CY2026"
claims.fix: Replace 'with a September 2026 General Availability date' with 'with General Availability targeted for September CY2026'; the status remains Rolling out.

claims.claim: The roadmap publishes no preview date.
claims.quote: "previewDate": null

claims.claim: The roadmap record was modified on September 1, 2026 at 23:00:02.
When web search is enabled, Copilot and Copilot Chat can ground responses in public web information.
claims.quote: When web search is enabled, Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Chat may fetch information from the Bing search service when information from the web helps to provide a better, more grounded response.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Administrators can configure up to 1,000 sites for domain exclusion.
claims.quote: By using domain exclusion, you can specify up to 1,000 sites to exclude from web grounding in Microsoft Copilot and Copilot Chat through a PowerShell script.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Excluded sites must not be used or cited in web-grounded answers.
claims.quote: Currently, domain exclusions support filtering on web page results only. Results from other answer verticals, such as news, might still be cited.
claims.fix: Qualify the summary and body: domain exclusion filters web page results only; news and other answer verticals might still cite excluded sites. Remove language implying a comprehensive citation or acceptable-use block.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Domain exclusion supports up to two levels of subdomain.
claims.quote: Currently, the domain exclusion configuration supports up to two levels of subdomains.

claims.claim: ConfigureTenantDomainExclusions.ps1 is the management script and is downloadable at aka.ms/Copilot/DomainExclusionScript.
claims.quote: To manage the Copilot domain exclusion configuration for your tenant, use the ConfigureTenantDomainExclusions.ps1 PowerShell script. Download it at https://aka.ms/Copilot/DomainExclusionScript.

claims.where: What's changing; controls[0].note; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The script can get the current configuration and export it to CSV.
claims.quote:
Export the current domain exclusion configuration to a CSV file:
   .\ConfigureTenantDomainExclusions.ps1 -Get

claims.where: controls[0].api; What's changing; Governance controls: first row; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: ConfigureTenantDomainExclusions.ps1 -Create -FromFile <csv> creates the tenant domain exclusion configuration.
claims.quote:
Create your domain exclusion configuration from a CSV file:
   .\ConfigureTenantDomainExclusions.ps1 -Create -FromFile "input.csv"

claims.claim: The script supports updating the configuration from CSV.
claims.quote:
Update your current domain exclusion configuration with entries from a CSV file:
   .\ConfigureTenantDomainExclusions.ps1 -Update -FromFile "updated_domains.csv"

claims.claim: The script supports deleting the current configuration.
claims.quote:
Remove your current domain exclusion configuration:
   .\ConfigureTenantDomainExclusions.ps1 -Delete

claims.where: What's changing; controls[0].note; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The script supports generating a template CSV.
claims.quote:
Create a template CSV file to help you get started:
   .\ConfigureTenantDomainExclusions.ps1 -Template

claims.claim: There is no exclusion configuration by default and the tenant opts in by running the script.
claims.quote: Default settings don't include the domain exclusion configuration. Opt in to use the feature by running the PowerShell script.

claims.claim: The feature's default-state classification is off.
claims.quote: Default settings don't include the domain exclusion configuration. Opt in to use the feature by running the PowerShell script.
claims.fix: Set defaultState to admin-opt-in. The standard assigns that classification to a new control that restricts nothing until an administrator configures it.

claims.claim: Cowork honours the same domain exclusion policies.
claims.quote: Cowork uses your organization's domain exclusion policies, including exclusions for specific domains.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls: first row and following paragraph; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented an admin UI for domain exclusion.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot" "domain exclusion" "admin center". Opened domain-exclusion and configure-copilot-admin-center on Microsoft Learn; these document the script, not a domain-exclusion UI.

claims.claim: The domain exclusion script requires Search Administrator or Global Administrator.
claims.quote: Sign in as a Search Administrator or Global Administrator.

claims.claim: The domain exclusion script needs the Az.Accounts module.
claims.quote: Az.Accounts PowerShell module (the ConfigureTenantDomainExclusions.ps1 script installs the module automatically if it's missing).

claims.claim: The exact Microsoft 365 Apps admin center path is Cloud Policy > Allow web search in Copilot.
claims.quote:
Under Customization, select Policy Management.
On the Policy configurations page, select Create.
claims.fix: Replace the path with 'Customization > Policy Management > Policy configurations > Create > Start with the basics > Choose the scope > Configure Settings > Allow web search in Copilot'. Cite overview-cloud-policy for navigation and manage-public-web-access for the setting; the existing docs link alone does not give the path.

claims.claim: An API or PowerShell equivalent for Allow web search in Copilot is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Allow web search in Copilot" "PowerShell" Graph API. Opened manage-public-web-access and overview-cloud-policy on Microsoft Learn; neither provides a management API or cmdlet for this policy.

claims.where: controls[1].scope and note; What's changing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Allow web search in Copilot is a Cloud Policy control for users or groups across the tenant.
claims.quote: This policy allows IT admins to either turn on or turn off web search for users or user groups across the tenant they manage in accordance with their organization's policies, data privacy laws, or other regulatory requirements.

claims.where: controls[1].note; What's changing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The web search policy supports enabling web search, disabling it, or disabling it in work mode only.
claims.quote:
Enabled in Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Chat
Disabled in Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Chat
Disabled in Microsoft Copilot Work mode; Enabled in Microsoft Copilot Web mode and Microsoft Copilot Chat

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; controls[2].governs
claims.claim: Purview DLP can block external web search when prompt text contains configured sensitive information types.
claims.quote: When a user prompt contains the configured SITs, Copilot and Cowork block external web search as a grounding source and continue to generate the response using allowed internal Microsoft 365 data sources.

claims.claim: The Purview configuration path goes directly from Custom to location Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork.
claims.quote:
Select the Custom template, then Custom policy.
On the Locations page, set the Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork location to on.
claims.fix: Use 'Data Loss Prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Custom > Custom policy > Locations > Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork'. Explain that a rule must use 'Content contains > Sensitive information types' and 'Prevent Copilot from processing content > Performing Web Searches', then save and turn on the policy.

claims.claim: New-DlpCompliancePolicy -Name <name> -Locations <location> -EnforcementPlanes @('CopilotExperiences') implements the sensitive-content web-search blocking control.
claims.quote: The fourth command creates the DLP policy using the $loc variable for the value of the Locations parameter, and "Copilot Policy" as the name of the policy (use any unique name).
claims.fix: The cmdlet, all three parameters and CopilotExperiences value exist in Security & Compliance PowerShell, but this creates only a policy container. Label it 'policy creation only; also configure a sensitive-information rule with the Performing Web Searches action' rather than presenting it as an equivalent blocking command.

claims.claim: Microsoft includes domain exclusion among its proactive prompt-injection defences.
claims.quote: Domain exclusion | Administrators can use a PowerShell script to exclude up to 1,000 sites from web grounding in Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: Web grounding sends a derived search query to the search provider.
claims.quote: Based on these terms, Copilot generates a search query that it sends to the Bing search service asking for more information.

claims.claim: The web search query does not contain Graph data.
claims.quote: Copilot finds the name of the user's manager from Microsoft 365 data. It then generates a Bing search query based on their name to see what information about them is available on the web.
claims.fix: Replace 'not Graph data' with 'not entire Microsoft 365 files; generated search terms can be informed by organizational data, including document content or a manager name'.

claims.claim: Prompts leave the tenant unless the Purview DLP web-search action stops them.
claims.quote: The user's prompts and Copilot's responses are stored within Microsoft 365 and never leave the service boundary for both Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Chat without customer direction.
claims.fix: Say 'Domain exclusion filters incoming web results; it does not prevent generated search queries being sent to Bing. Purview DLP can block external web search when prompt text matches configured sensitive information types.' Distinguish derived queries from full prompts; very short prompts can themselves form the query.

claims.claim: The script can be run by an administrator with the appropriate Copilot or Global admin role.
claims.quote: Sign in as a Search Administrator or Global Administrator.
claims.fix: Replace 'appropriate Copilot or Global admin role' with 'Search Administrator or Global Administrator', matching the documented prerequisites and the table note.

claims.claim: Users will not be told why a site was not cited.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot" "domain exclusion" "notification". Opened domain-exclusion and manage-public-web-access on Microsoft Learn; neither states how domain-exclusion notifications work.
claims.fix: Remove the assertion or write 'Microsoft has not documented domain-exclusion user messaging at the time of writing (November 2026).' Keep the advice to publish the policy internally.

claims.claim: Wildcard-style blocking of whole top-level domains is not described.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot" "domain exclusion" "wildcard"; Copilot domain exclusion declarative agents scoped web search excluded sites notification wildcard TLD. Opened domain-exclusion; no wildcard or whole-TLD syntax is documented.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Domain exclusion is included and requires no additional licence.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot domain exclusion licensing pricing admin UI ConfigureTenantDomainExclusions; "Copilot" "domain exclusion" "license" "cost". Opened domain-exclusion and read licensing search excerpts; no feature-specific inclusion statement was found.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to unknown. Replace 'No additional licence' and 'No licence' with 'Feature-specific licensing is not yet published; the documented script prerequisites name roles, PowerShell and CSV requirements but no licence.'

claims.claim: Domain exclusion has no metered cost.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot domain exclusion licensing pricing admin UI ConfigureTenantDomainExclusions; "Copilot" "domain exclusion" "license" "cost". Opened domain-exclusion and read Plan licensing and cost search excerpts; none states domain exclusion is unmetered.
claims.fix: Replace 'No licence or metered cost' with 'Feature-specific licensing and pricing are not yet published; no domain-exclusion meter is documented at the time of writing (November 2026).'

claims.claim: The cost classification is none because configuration uses a script.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot domain exclusion licensing pricing admin UI ConfigureTenantDomainExclusions; "Copilot" "domain exclusion" "license" "cost". Read the roadmap record and domain-exclusion; neither states inclusion in existing licences.
claims.fix: Set cost to low. Use the rationale 'Low. Maintaining the CSV and running the script take administrator time; feature-specific licensing and pricing are not yet published.' Script-based configuration is not evidence for the standard's none classification.

claims.claim: Government tenants have web search off by default.
claims.quote: By default, web search is enabled for Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Chat in commercial tenants, but not for U.S. Government Community Cloud (GCC, GCC-High, and DoD) tenants.

claims.claim: Government clouds are not listed for this roadmap item.
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.claim: Domain exclusion does not apply to declarative agents' scoped web search sites.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot domain exclusion declarative agents scoped web search excluded sites notification wildcard TLD. Opened domain-exclusion and knowledge-sources on Microsoft Learn; neither states this exemption.
claims.fix: Remove the assertion that domain exclusion does not apply to declarative agents' scoped web search sites. Say 'Microsoft has not documented how tenant domain exclusions interact with declarative agents that scope web search to an excluded site at the time of writing (November 2026).' Retain this as an open question.

claims.claim: Declarative agents can configure scoped web search sites in their manifest.
claims.quote: To scope your web search to specific sites, add the sites property and specify up to four URLs, as shown in the following example.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/knowledge-sources#web-and-scoped-web-search to sources for the manifest statement. It does not establish an exemption from tenant exclusions.

claims.claim: The domain exclusion list is not visible in Cloud Policy.
claims.quote: Searched: "domain exclusion" "Cloud Policy" "admin center"; "Copilot" "domain exclusion" "admin center". Opened domain-exclusion, configure-copilot-admin-center and overview-cloud-policy; none states whether the exclusion list is visible there.
claims.fix: Replace the visibility assertion with 'Microsoft documents domain exclusion management through the PowerShell script at the time of writing (November 2026).'

claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 admin center links to web search policy management under Copilot > Settings > Data access.
claims.quote: Follow the link from Copilot settings to create an Allow web search in Copilot cloud policy in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center.

claims.claim: The web search setting is configured in Cloud Policy rather than on the Microsoft 365 Copilot settings page.
claims.quote: The primary way that IT admins can control access to web search is by using the Allow web search in Copilot policy, which is available only in Cloud Policy service for Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: Copilot users can turn web search off personally when administrators allow it, but cannot turn it on when policy disables it.
claims.quote: If the IT admin turns off web search, the Web content toggle is turned off and appears dimmed. Users can't turn on the toggle to use web search.

claims.where: Open questions; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Feature-specific government cloud availability has not been published beyond the roadmap's commercial listing.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot" "domain exclusion" "GCC". Opened domain-exclusion and read government-cloud search excerpts; none establishes domain-exclusion availability for government tenants. The roadmap lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant) only.
